text:
The sugar beet crop in the Tavrin Valley failed this season, the Tavrin Valley Agricultural Board confirmed on 14 October 2024.

The finding is set out in the Board's "Autumn Harvest Assessment Report (TVAB-24/09)", which was released at a press briefing in the town of Karsholm. According to the report, sugar beet yields fell 62 per cent below the five-year average, with about 18,400 hectares affected.

Dr. Marek Oslavin, the Board's Chief Agronomist, presented the assessment at the briefing. The report designates the season's sugar beet harvest an official failure, the formal step that follows the Board's autumn field assessments.

The Board's report is the basis for the figures cited here. This newspaper has not independently verified the yield data or the affected acreage.
